title: Ang 1430: the last page
hookLine: the walk through the Granth is complete
tomorrow: why would anyone set an alarm for the dark before dawn?

lines: AFTER THE SEAL: A LIST OF RAGAS.
cards: Stay in your seat after a movie ends and the credits roll: the names of everyone who made the sound. The Guru Granth Sahib has something a little like that.
After the seal comes the last page, and on it isn't another hymn. It's a list of ragas, the musical modes, set out in families, mode after mode. A holy book that closes with a music list.

teach.h: THE RAAGMALA: A GARLAND OF RAGAS.
teach.b: The page is called the Raagmala, a garland of ragas.

First, an honest part of the puzzle: Sikhs hold different views about it. Some read it aloud at the end of a full reading. Others close at the Mundavani and hold that the Raagmala isn't the Gurus' own bani.
It sits in the printed Granth either way, and the question isn't settled among Sikhs. Now the solution, the part nobody disputes. Walk back through the whole book and see how it's built.
After the opening prayers, the hymns are arranged by raga: Sri Rag, Majh, Gauri, Asa, on through the last raga, Jaijavanti.
The Granth is a songbook. Its words were made to be sung, in kirtan, in a particular mood of music. So whatever you hold about the Raagmala, the last page points at the music the whole Guru lives in.
And it is a whole Guru.

teach.h: THE GRANTH AS THE LIVING GURU.
teach.b: Tradition says Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Guru, passed the guruship to the Granth, and Sikhs bow to it as the living Guru, not a book about one.
When a full reading ends, Sikhs often sing Anand Sahib, say Ardas, and share karah prashad. The walk is finished. Every page, from the first line to the last.

how: When a full reading of the Guru Granth Sahib ends, the congregation sings Anand Sahib, an Ardas is said, a hukam is taken and karah prashad is shared; congregations differ on whether the Raagmala is read before the close.

o: the last page: a list of ragas, and the walk's end
the page where Kabir's couplets come to a close
the page of Guru Arjan's plate of three things

games.q: a friend from orchestra flips to the end of an English Granth and asks why a holy book closes with a list of musical modes. what's the best short answer?
o: the hymns are arranged by raga: it's a songbook, made to be sung.
it's an index, so readers can quickly find their favorite hymns.
it's a page every Sikh skips, so it doesn't really matter at all.
games.why: whatever a reader holds about the Raagmala, the book is built raga by raga, and the last page names the music it lives in.

practice: If you have a recording of Anand Sahib, play its opening and just listen. Its first line, in paraphrase: joy has come, mother, for I have found the True Guru. Let the music end, and let the sit hold the quiet after it.

wordCard.voice: Ang 1430. The last page: the Raagmala's list of ragas, read by some and closed before by others, and the end of the walk.

carryVoice: To keep: the whole guru, first page to last, every one walked. That's a long road, and it's done.
